definitions.explanation: Considering all aspects or the entire scope of something. Used to make broad assessments or summaries rather than commenting on specific details.

examples.japanese: {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{良|よ}い{結果|けっか}だった。
{今年|ことし}の{業績|ぎょうせき}は{全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{好調|こうちょう}だ。
examples.english: This year's performance is generally strong.

examples.japanese: {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{見|み}て、この{計画|けいかく}は{成功|せいこう}と{言|い}えるだろう。
examples.english: Looking at it overall, this plan can be called a success.

notes:
USAGE:
Formed from {全般|ぜんぱん} (the whole, everything) + {的|てき} (adjectival suffix) + に (adverbial particle). Often placed at the beginning of a sentence or before a verb/adjective to qualify a broad judgment. The base adjective form {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}な can also modify nouns: {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}な{傾向|けいこう} (overall tendency).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{見|み}て (looking at it overall)
- {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{好調|こうちょう} (generally strong/favorable)
- {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}な{傾向|けいこう} (overall tendency)
- {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{言|い}えば (generally speaking)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{概|おおむ}ね (generally, mostly) is similar but slightly more formal. {総合的|そうごうてき}に (comprehensively) emphasizes combining multiple factors into a whole assessment.
